placements.why: The content names an organizational category — the practice of bringing an instrument from unverified to verified state against reference standards — that nothing in the existing (empty) strata covers. Calibration is a recognized strata category for this org, and this envelope's content is the first real instance requiring it.
placements.title: From unverified to verified instrument state
placements.frame: How is instrument accuracy established and checked against reference standards?

placements.title: Reference-plate verification settles instrument accuracy
placements.frame: What does it take for an instrument's calibration to be accepted as holding across its observing band?
placements.why: Both segments perform the same thematic content: the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration is established at 88.4 MHz and verified against June reference plates, with the lead astronomer asserting it holds across the full observing band. This is a thematic container for calibration-verification events — future envelopes may feed it with subsequent calibration checks, band-coverage assertions, or reference-plate comparisons — not a one-time fact. The specific 88.4 MHz value and June plates are evidence for this theme, not a leaf themselves.
